$comment: Minimum wages California sets by INDUSTRY rather than by geography. They are not local ordinances and not the state minimum wage; a covered fast-food or health-care employee is owed the sectoral rate even in a city with no local ordinance at all, and even where the local ordinance is lower.

sectors.name: Fast food restaurant employees
sectors.coverage: Employees of limited-service restaurants that are part of a national chain with 60 or more establishments nationwide (AB 1228 / Labor Code 1475 et seq.), as set by the Fast Food Council.
sectors.note: Unchanged at $20.00 for 2026 -- the Council has adopted no increase since the rate took effect.

sectors.name: Health care workers -- large health systems, large hospitals and dialysis clinics
sectors.coverage: SB 525 (Health & Safety Code 1182.14 et seq.) covered employees of large private hospitals, large integrated health systems and dialysis clinics.

sectors.name: Health care workers -- other covered facilities, including skilled nursing facilities
sectors.coverage: SB 525 covered employees at facilities outside the large-system, high-government-payor and clinic categories.
sectors.note: Stepped to $23.00 on 2026-07-01, continuing toward $25.00 later in the SB 525 schedule.

sectors.name: Los Angeles hotel workers
sectors.coverage: Employees at Los Angeles hotels with 60 or more guest rooms, under the city's Hotel Worker Minimum Wage Ordinance as amended in 2026.

healthBenefitSupplement.note: An ADDITIONAL $4.25/hr for the provision of health care benefits; where the employer provides no health benefits, the $4.25 must be paid as additional hourly wages -- so the cash floor is $29.25.

sources.title: California employment-law summaries of the July 1, 2026 sectoral wage steps (Fisher Phillips, CalChamber, SHRM, California Medical Association)
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session across several independent California employment-law summaries for the fast-food $20.00, the SB 525 steps to $25.00 (large systems, hospitals and dialysis) and $23.00 (other covered facilities including skilled nursing) on 2026-07-01, and the Los Angeles hotel-worker $25.00 plus the $4.25 health-benefit supplement. The URL given is one of those summaries -- its own rate CHART is a PDF this session could not render, so the figures rest on the agreeing prose of several sources rather than on that chart. California DIR's own health-care minimum wage FAQ 404'd on a direct fetch. This is the weakest-sourced file in this database and is marked accordingly.

knownGaps: SB 525 defines FOUR employer categories. Only the two whose 2026-07-01 figures were confirmed this session are asserted here; the high-government-payor/rural-independent hospital category and the clinic category exist and are on their own slower schedules, and no figure is guessed for them.

Los Angeles also sets an airport-worker minimum wage, and Santa Monica, Long Beach, West Hollywood and Glendale each run hotel-worker ordinances. Those are real minimum wages that are deliberately NOT given figures here, because none was verified to a primary or double-secondary standard this session.
Whether a particular restaurant or facility is 'covered' is a legal determination under each statute's own definitions; this file carries rates, not coverage tests.
